name: Cover Story
tagline: The current issue of a magazine about one company, with stickers you can peel off and slap anywhere.
summary: The homepage is a magazine cover you can open: a three.js cover that bends on its spine, a real magnifying glass that magnifies its print, and a glass crystal rising from the inside spread, which turns the story column into a contents page. Editorial serif and NASA crystal photography carry the gravitas; neo-brutalist stickers carry every fact from content.js, and visitors can peel them off a sticker sheet and put them on the page themselves. It reads as someone with taste and range who ships, never as a bank or a consultancy.
voice: Editorial and dry, an amused magazine writing about a serious subject. Example: "Small products, shipped, then left to compound."
motion: Stickers slap down with an overshoot and their hard shadows land a beat later, while paper turns slowly on its spine. Everything else holds still.
sound: Off by default. When it is on, the sounds are made from filtered noise: a short thump when a sticker lands, a bright swish when one peels off, and a breath of air when the cover turns.
mark: A violet sticker with an Archivo 'A' whose corner peels back to a lime underside, the same gesture as opening the cover.
